To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spin‐crossover transition of [FeL  2][BF  4]  2 ⋅ Me  2 CO is accompanied by a crystallographic transition from phase 1 to phase 2.
a crystal structure with a Z′ of 1 undergoes a spin transition that is incomplete, and that the crystal structure of the spin crossover compound changes from a Z′ of one to one of 24.
the spin transition in [FeL2][BF4](2)⋅Me(2)CO is associated with a Z=4→Z=48 crystallographic symmetry breaking.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the spin‐crossover phenomenon, which is a reversible change in the spin state of a metal centre in response to an external stimulus.
the design and synthesis of a new series of iron(II) spin crossover (SCO) complexes with the general formula [FeL2][BF4].
the study of the spin crossover in a new class of Fe(II) complexes with N,N′-chelating ligands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystallographic symmetry breaking in [FeL  n][BF4]n is associated with the onset of spin‐crossover, and the symmetry breaking in [ClO4]n is not associated with spin‐crossover.

the crystallographic symmetry of [FeL  2][BF4 ]2 ⋅ Me2CO changes from phase 1 to phase 2 at T1/2, and this is accompanied by an incomplete spin transition from the HS state to a mixture of HS and LS states.
the crystallographic phase transitions in the [BF4]2 salt are associated with the spin crossover but the reverse is not true.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a crystallographic symmetry breaking from Z′=1 to Z′=24 is accompanied by an incomplete spin transition.
the spin transition is associated with the formation of a crystallographic superlattice with a Z′ factor of 12.
a spin transition is accompanied by a Z′=4→Z′=48 crystallographic symmetry breaking, whereas a crystallographic symmetry breaking from Z′=4 to Z′=8 is not accompanied by a spin transition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spin crossover is not a necessary condition for the formation of the Z′=48 phase.
the crystallographic symmetry change from P21/c to P21 is not sufficient to cause a full spin crossover in this system.
a crystallographic Z′=1 to Z′=24 symmetry breaking can be associated with a 50 % spin transition.
